assumptions: Γ a finite set of finitary relations on D
attrs.evidence: Derived from standard finite-CSP algebra: every finite structure has a core (Hell–Nešetřil 1992); endomorphisms preserve pp-definable relations; the canonical conjunctive query at an element of a finite core pp-defines its automorphism orbit. (⇐) transitivity makes every non-empty pp-definable unary relation contain the whole core. (⇒) two orbits give two disjoint non-empty pp-definable unary relations. Checked on nine languages against the symmetry certificate and the bounded search, with no disagreement on any conclusive result.
attrs.prior_art: Ingredients standard — Hell–Nešetřil 1992 (cores); Bodirsky, Graph Homomorphisms and Universal Algebra Prop. 5.10 (pp-definable orbits); Jeavons–Cohen–Gyssens 1997 (Inv–Pol). NOVELTY OF THE EQUIVALENCE IS NOT CLAIMED and no exact prior-art search has been done: publish it as "the constraint template has a transitive core", derived here, not as a named classical theorem.
attrs.review_focus: The equivalence is short and its ingredients are textbook, which is exactly the profile of a result someone has already published. FED-1PA-NAME is the search, and it is still open.
attrs.statement: Γ has the one-variable gluing property (working-1PA) if and only if the automorphism group of the core of (D; Γ) acts transitively on the core.
